name: l1-review-clock-v1
idea_origin: Leah's local scripted sweep (1,562 games, lab/panel) and the race's score gap (lab/panel/README.md)
hypothesis: The race survives but does not grow: completed games average 13.8/30 on level and 6.9/20 on wealth, and over half of all eliminations are the capability dismissal after weak reviews. Leah's scripted sweep found that the best quarterly plan was a preventive Health reserve, then Prepare report materials, with Apply for a key project as the default main action, and that High-intensity work was the worst Energy choice. A manual that plans every quarter around the published review and promotion cadence, grows Skill, Network and Output together (the published promotion factors), keeps a Health reserve before it is needed and reads the HR remark as a risk gauge should promote earlier and more often than the reactive F3 leader, while surviving as often.
change: New single Skill, review-clock, about 390 words. Four rules: a preventive Health reserve in every Energy phase; the HR remark and warnings as a risk gauge driving Defuse legacy risk and Lay low; a window plan with Apply for a key project as the default main action, a catch-up action for whichever of Skill, Network or Output trails, Prepare report materials for spare Energy and no High-intensity work; story events judged on honest, scoped delivery versus hiding, blaming or overcommitting.
predicted_behaviour: Health stays in the upper part of its range in most quarters; Energy goes to Health recovery first and Prepare report materials second; High-intensity work never appears; Apply for a key project is the main action in most quarters; Defuse legacy risk follows a worried HR remark within the next Energy phase. Promotions arrive at the first or second window more often than in F3 runs, and the level dimension of completed games is higher than F3's.
refutation: Refuted if, with the same Haiku actor, the mean quantitative_score is below f3-feedback-reactive-v1's or the completion rate drops (growth bought with survival). Refuted on mechanism if the level dimension of completed games is not higher than F3's. The text is not being executed if High-intensity work appears, if notes stop naming the reserve, risk tone and window plan, or if Health is often in the lower part of its range at quarter end.
notes: Written by Leah (26 Oct, branch leah/workspace) without copying event text or answers. No numbers, months, event titles or unpublished thresholds: the six-monthly review and promotion window, the promotion factors, the action names and their published effects, and the 0-10 range are all public (rules.rst, handbook.rst). First read: 5 Haiku games under origin leah on Leah's Mac (CLI 2.1.295, Pro account), so not the race's actor cell.
